title: Lift a service door off its lift-off hinges once it is open past about 80 degrees
instruction: Take the service door off the unit and stand it in the door rack.
context: HVAC mechanics take service doors off rooftop units and air handlers to reach the blower and coil (O*NET 49-9021). The doors hang on lift-off pins; a tab on the hinge sleeve runs under a keeper so a part-open door cannot be knocked off, and lines up with the keeper's notch only near full open. Unlike TK-JG9NPW (hang a door on a pin hinge) and TK-VNC9LD (lift a fire door's hook), the robot must swing the door to where it clears, then lift it off.
setup: Directions are from the robot: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'right' is toward the right arm, heights are above the table top, the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Unit (fixed, grey painted sheet steel): a closed box 106 mm front to back, 197 mm wide and 128 mm tall, its front face 39.4 cm in front of the arm bases, spanning 23.2 to 3.5 cm right of the midline. Hinge, on a vertical axis 36.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 22.0 cm right of the midline: a grey steel collar 22 mm across from the table to 12 mm; a dark (black oxide) steel lower pin 10 mm across from 12 to 37 mm; a grey steel upper leaf 12 mm wide and 7 mm thick at 67 to 74 mm, running from 6 mm nearer the robot than the axis to the unit's face; a dark steel upper pin 10 mm across from 74 to 99 mm. Keeper (fixed, grey steel plate 5 mm thick, 102 to 107 mm up) just above the upper hinge, carried from the unit's face by two arms 18 mm long: it covers a ring 13.5 to 28 mm from the hinge axis except a notch. Measuring directions about the axis seen from above, 0 degrees pointing away from the robot and 90 degrees toward the robot's left, it covers -100 to -29 degrees and 21 to 50 degrees, built as straight segments. Door (loose, 120 g, cream painted steel panel 151 x 10 x 100 mm, from 9 mm to 160 mm out from the hinge axis, bottom edge 12 mm up, top edge 112 mm up): on its hinge edge two square grey steel sleeves, 18 mm outside, 12 mm square hole, 18 mm tall, at 12 to 30 mm and 78 to 96 mm up, over the lower and upper pins. The upper sleeve has a tab 4 mm wide, 6 mm tall (90 to 96 mm up), reaching from 9 to 24 mm out from the axis on the side away from the panel. The door hangs with its lower sleeve on the collar, standing 30 degrees open (free edge swung toward the robot); its tab sits 6 mm under the keeper and lines up with the notch only between about 80 and 95 degrees open. Door stop (fixed, dark steel post 12 mm across, 25 mm tall) at 30.1 cm in front of the arm bases and 27.5 cm right of the midline; the open door meets it at about 125 degrees. Door rack (fixed, yellow plastic): two walls 120 mm long, 10 mm thick and 50 mm tall, running front to back from 21.5 to 33.5 cm in front of the arm bases, with an 18 mm slot between them centred 33.0 cm right of the midline; the slot floor is the table. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Pass/fail. 1.0 when all of these hold at once for 1 second: the door is off both pins (neither sleeve has its centre less than 19 mm from the hinge axis sideways while reaching to within 5 mm of its pin's height range); it stands in the rack, with the lowest corner of the panel at most 3 mm above the table, the panel within 10 degrees of upright (its top and bottom edges within 10 degrees of level, either way up and either end first), and the middle of its bottom edge between the rack's walls (within 9 mm of the slot's centre line) and within the rack's 120 mm length; no gripper finger or gripper body is within 5 mm of the door; and the door is still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Otherwise 0: the door still on a pin or jammed with its tab under the keeper, held in the air, dropped on the table, lying across the rack's walls, leaning more than 10 degrees, resting on a wall top, or still gripped.
reset_notes: Lift the door out of the rack, drop its sleeves over both pins so the lower sleeve rests on the collar, and swing it to 30 degrees open (free edge 8.0 cm nearer the robot than the hinge axis). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders in PhysX. Sleeves are square, not round barrels, with 1 mm of play per side on the pins. The tab and keeper are a simple version of a lift-off hinge's retaining tab; the 80 to 95 degree window is chosen, not taken from a product. The door is 120 g and 16 cm wide, much lighter and smaller than a real one. One fixed layout: a replay of the demo's waypoints would pass.
